name: Progress
hint: Switch to indeterminate: it drifts calmly instead of racing.
description: Linear bar, ring or segmented steps, determinate or indeterminate. Indeterminate states drift and breathe rather than race; values spring and the percentage rolls like an odometer, becoming a check at 100%.
usage: Use determinate whenever you know the fraction: pass `value` (and `max` if it is not 100) with a `label` that says what is happening; `hint` adds a line under it. Use `indeterminate` only for unknown waits under ~10s. For a sequence pass `kind="steps"` with `steps` (a count or an array of step labels) and `current` (0-based). `valueText` replaces the readout and what screen readers hear ("3 of 5 done"). For a usage meter (seats used, storage) pass `showComplete={false}` and `width="100%"`. Nothing loops at rest; with no props it renders an empty bar.
screenReader: A role="progressbar" named by `label` (or an aria-label you pass), with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and an aria-valuetext of the percent, "Step 2 of 5: <step>", "Complete" or your `valueText`. Indeterminate drops aria-valuenow, sets aria-busy and reads "Working" (or `valueText`).

dataProps.description: Which progress: "linear" is a bar with a label and a readout, "ring" is a circle with the readout in its centre (sized by `size`), "steps" is a bar cut into segments (see `steps` and `current`).
How far along, from 0 to `max`. Ignored when `indeterminate` is on or when steps get a `current`.
Unknown progress: a calm drifting band (ring: a breathing arc). The only state that moves on its own.
What is happening ("Uploading 3 files"). Names the progressbar for screen readers. Without it, pass `aria-label`.
Second line under the bar ("12 of 19 files").

dataProps.type: string | ((info: { value: number; max: number; percent: number; step: number; steps: number; current: number; done: boolean; busy: boolean }) => string)
dataProps.description: Replaces the visible readout and the aria-valuetext. A function gets { value, max, percent, step, steps, current, done, busy }. Use it for checklists ("3 of 5 done") or units ("18 of 20 seats").
Steps kind: the number of segments, or the steps themselves (their labels go to the tooltip and to screen readers).
Steps kind: the 0-based index of the step you are on. Setting it (or passing `steps` as an array) makes the bar step-by-step instead of value-driven; current = steps.length means all done.
At 100% turn green, draw a check and swap in the done copy. Right for a task that finishes; set false for a meter (plan usage, storage) so 100% stays a number in its tone.
Label shown at 100% when showComplete is on. "" keeps your label.
Hint shown at 100% when showComplete is on. "" keeps your hint.
Widest the bar grows: px as a number, or any CSS length. "100%" fills the container.
Diameter of the ring (kind "ring"): sm 60px, md 72px, lg 96px. The centre readout is 20% of it. A number sets the diameter in px exactly.
Fill empty label and hints with the gallery's sample upload copy. Leave off in real UI.
The root element, for measuring or scrolling to.
Any other attribute (id, aria-*, data-*) goes to the root <div>. className and style are merged with the component's own.

example:
<Progress
  label="Uploading 3 files"
  hint="About 20 seconds left"
  value={bytesSent}
  max={bytesTotal}
/>

<Progress kind="steps" steps={["Account", "Workspace", "Invite"]} current={step} label="Setting up" />

<Progress label="Seats used" value={18} max={20} valueText="18 of 20 seats" tone="warning" showComplete={false} width="100%" />
